content: Metronidazole is a medication prescribed to treat acne rosacea, a chronic condition characterized by inflammation of the facial skin and the development of sores. While it helps reduce redness and the number of sores, it may not completely cure the condition. Additionally, it is used to treat certain vaginal infections. In some cases, your doctor may prescribe it for other uses, so consult them or your pharmacist for further information. Metronidazole is available as a gel for application on the skin or for use in the vagina. For most conditions, it is typically applied twice daily. When treating vaginal infections, it is used twice daily for five consecutive days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use metronidazole exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. If you are using it for acne, you may notice improvement within three weeks, with continued progress over six weeks or more. Do not stop using the medication without consulting your doctor, as discontinuing it may worsen your symptoms. For acne treatment, cleanse the affected skin with mild soap 15–20 minutes before applying the medication. Apply a thin layer of the gel and gently rub it into the affected area. Avoid contact with your eyes. After application, you may use a moisturizer (if your skin is dry) and cosmetics, but consult your doctor for advice on suitable products. The vaginal gel comes with a special applicator. Follow these steps for proper use: 1. Fill the applicator to the indicated level. 2. Lie on your back with your knees bent and spread apart. 3. Gently insert the applicator into your vagina and push the plunger to release the medication. 4. Remove the applicator and wash it with soap and warm water. 5. Wash your hands immediately to prevent spreading the infection. Apply the vaginal gel at bedtime, as the medication works best when you remain lying down afterward. You may wear a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use tampons, as they can absorb the medication. Avoid douching while using this medication, as it can wash the drug out of the vagina and reduce its effectiveness. Continue using the medication even if you get your period during treatment. Before using metronidazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants like warfarin and any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have had central nervous system disease, liver or blood disorders, or Crohn's disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using metronidazole, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as metronidazole may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not consume alcohol while using the vaginal gel, as it may cause adverse effects such as stomach upset, vomiting, stomach cramps, headaches, sweating, and facial flushing. If you forget to apply a dose of the acne gel, do so as soon as you remember, but do not apply a double dose to make up for the missed one. If you miss a dose of the vaginal gel, apply it the next morning or night and continue with your usual dosing schedule. Metronidazole may cause side effects. Contact your doctor if you experience increased skin redness, dryness, burning, irritation, or stinging. If you experience severe side effects such as stomach pain, fever, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Metronidazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Refrain from sexual intercourse during the five days of vaginal gel use. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. If your symptoms persist after completing the treatment, contact your doctor.
